query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of Ti into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3
generation.intervention: Introduction of a controlled amount of Ti
generation.conditions: Room temperature, exposure to air, and high-temperature oxidation environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable solid-solution phase with refined grain structure
generation.mechanism: Ti addition strengthens the alloy and increases its ability to withstand extremes of temperature, leading to improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.boundary: Ti content: 5-15 at%, temperature: 20-1000°C, exposure time: 1-100 hours
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Ti required to achieve optimal properties is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled addition of Ti to the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy, followed by characterization of microstructure, compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
measurements: Microstructure analysis using XRD and TEM
Compressive behavior testing using universal testing machine
Corrosion resistance testing using potentiodynamic polarization
High-temperature oxidation resistance testing using thermogravimetry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of Ti does not lead to improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
